title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Jordan Lee
content:
Summary:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and contractors who need to follow consistent processes that protect customer data, maintain operational stability, and simplify approvals.

Table of contents:
1. Access and permissions
2. Change management
3. Data management and classification
4. Procurement and expenses
5. Vendor management and onboarding
6. Travel and expenses policy (travel)
7. Internal templates and examples
8. Contacts and escalation

1) Access and permissions
Purpose: Enforce least privilege, ensure auditable provisioning/deprovisioning, and reduce blast radius from compromised accounts.
Scope: All corporate accounts, cloud console access, internal admin interfaces, and third-party SaaS connected to Redwood systems.
Owners: Security (security@redwood.com) and People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).

Policy highlights:
- Principle of least privilege: role-based access controls (RBAC) are required; do not grant wide/global roles without documented justification and timebox.
- Onboarding: access requests must be submitted via the Access Request form in the IT ticketing system (link internal) and include role justification and manager approval.
- Offboarding: People Ops triggers an automated deprovisioning workflow when a termination or contract end is recorded; managers must confirm return of devices prior to final deactivation.
- Temporary elevated access: use Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation with approvals from service owner and Security; maximum elevation window is 8 hours unless exception is approved by Security.
- Privileged credential handling: secrets must be stored in the company vault (KMS/HashiCorp Vault). Hardcoding credentials in code or repositories is strictly prohibited.

Procedure (requesting access):
1. Open IT ticket: select the resource and justify access level.
2. Manager approval via ticket comments.
3. Security review for elevated permissions (if requested).
4. Access granted and recorded in the audit log with ticket ID.

SLA and audit cadence:
- Access requests: target 2 business days for standard requests; 8 business hours for emergency requests with on-call approval.
- Quarterly access reviews: resource owners must review role membership and certify or remediate within 14 days.

2) Change management
Purpose: Minimize service disruption and ensure safe rollouts across production, staging, and infra changes.
Scope: Any change that affects production services, infra configuration, network ACLs, or persistent data schemas.
Owners: Eng Platform and Eng SRE (eng-platform@redwood.com, eng-sre@redwood.com).

Change classification and required approvals:
- Standard change (low risk, pre-approved): routine patches, configuration tweaks that match pre-approved templates — change logged, no CAB approval.
- Normal change (planned): requires documented plan, pre-deployment runbook, rollback plan, and CAB approval for changes impacting >1% of customers or multiple services.
- Emergency change: implemented to address an active outage or critical security vulnerability; must be documented retrospectively and reviewed by postmortem.

Change process (normal):
1. Submit Change Request (CR) in the Change tracker with: summary, impact, roll-out plan, rollback plan, testing, and owner.
2. Automated risk assessment flags if CAB review is required.
3. CAB review window: weekly slots; CRs requiring CAB must be submitted 48 hours prior.
4. Post-deploy validation and monitoring checklist.
5. Close CR with evidence (logs, screenshots), and link to incident tracker if applicable.

Thresholds and guardrails:
- Any schema migration that alters table shape in production requires a canary rollout (5% traffic) and two-week monitoring window.
- Firewall/network ACL changes must be ticketed and scheduled in change windows unless emergency.

3) Data management and classification
Purpose: Ensure consistent handling of data, align retention and encryption policies with regulatory requirements, and reduce risk of data leakage.
Scope: Customer data, telemetry, PII, logs, backup snapshots, and configuration data.
Owners: Security and Product data governance (security@redwood.com, data-governance@redwood.com).

Classification levels:
- Public: can be published without restriction.
- Internal: internal-only materials; no external disclosure without approval.
- Confidential: customer-identifiable data; requires encryption at rest and in transit and stricter access control.
- Restricted: regulated or highly sensitive data (e.g., contractual secrets, keys); requires HSM/KMS management, strict logging, and legal OK for any access.

Retention and disposal:
- Logs (operational): retain 90 days in hot storage, 365 days in cold archive unless otherwise needed for compliance.
- Backups: immutable snapshots retained for 90 days by default.
- Customer data: adhere to contract-specific retention clauses; delete on customer request within contractual SLA.

Encryption and key management:
- All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest using company-managed KMS keys.
- Key rotation: keys rotated annually or after any suspected compromise.

Data handling checklist (developer-facing):
- Identify classification level before storing data.
- Use approved storage buckets and set lifecycle policies.
- Do not log raw PII; use tokenization or redaction.
- Use the secure transfer library (internal: libs/secure-transfer) for inter-service transfers.

4) Procurement and expenses
Purpose: Provide predictable procurement processes, cost control, and timely reimbursements.
Scope: All purchases using company funds, corporate cards, and employee expense reimbursements.
Owners: Finance and People Ops (finance@redwood.com, procurement@redwood.com).

Approval thresholds and methods:
- Up to $1,000: Manager approval, corporate card allowed for pre-approved categories.
- $1,001 – $25,000: Department head approval required; procurement should be engaged for vendor negotiation.
- > $25,000: Procurement + Finance + Legal review and a signed PO or contract.

Procurement process (summary):
1. Fill Procurement Request Template and attach vendor quote(s).
2. Department head approves in the procurement system.
3. Procurement reviews for vendor terms, negotiates pricing, and routes to Finance/Legal if > $25k.
4. Purchase executed via PO or corporate card as appropriate.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit expense report in the Expenses tool within 30 days of the expense.
- Required items: receipt, business purpose, project code, approver’s name.
- Reimbursement timeline: Finance processes within 10 business days of submission.

Corporate card policy:
- Cards issued on a case-by-case basis; cardholder training required.
- Personal charges are prohibited and will be treated as taxable income and subject to recovery.

5) Vendor management and onboarding
Purpose: Standardize vendor risk assessment, contract terms, and ongoing vendor monitoring.
Scope: Third-party SaaS providers, infrastructure vendors, professional services, and contractors.
Owners: Procurement and Legal (procurement@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com).

Onboarding checklist:
- Business case and owner identified.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- Data flow diagram and classification of data shared.
- Contract reviewed by Legal with SLAs and termination clauses.
- PO or SOW signed and recorded.

Ongoing monitoring:
- Quarterly vendor health check for strategic vendors.
- Annual security reassessment for vendors handling Confidential or Restricted data.
- Maintain a vendor registry with contract end dates and renewal reminders.

6) Travel policy (business travel)
Purpose: Keep travelers safe, control travel spend, and ensure timely expense reconciliation.
Scope: All business travel booked by employees or contractors on Redwood’s behalf.
Owners: People Ops and Finance (people-ops@redwood.com, finance@redwood.com).

Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked through the approved travel vendor or with People Ops assistance.
- Travel > $3,000 requires Director-level approval.
- International travel requires a travel safety review and manager sign-off at least 10 business days prior.

Per diem and allowable expenses:
- Meals: use per diem caps by region (see appendix link).
- Lodging: book in business class hotels; upgrades require justification and manager approval.
- Ground transport: use ride-share or approved car services; rental cars require Collision Damage Waiver unless exempted.

Traveler safety:
- Register international trips with People Ops and provide emergency contact info.
- Employees must carry the emergency travel card and follow travel advisory instructions.

7) Internal templates and examples
Included below are short, copy/paste templates for common use. Use the company template repository for full versions.

A) Procurement request template (short):
- Title: [Brief procurement title]
- Department: [Department name]
- Owner: [Name, email]
- Estimated cost: [$]
- Vendor: [Vendor name]
- Business justification: [Why we need it]
- Approvals: [Manager name]

B) Expense report template (short):
- Employee: [Name]
- Date of expense: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Category: [Travel / Meals / Supplies]
- Amount: [$]
- Receipt: [attached yes/no]
- Project/code: [Project code]

C) Access request template (short):
- Name: [User]
- Role: [Role title]
- Resource(s): [Service / console / repo]
- Justification: [Business need]
- Manager approval: [Name]

D) Change Request minimum fields:
- Change title, owner, impact, roll-out plan, rollback steps, test plan, monitoring checklist, scheduled window, CAB required (yes/no)

8) Contacts and escalation
- People Ops (general): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security (access, incident reporting): security@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Finance (expenses): finance@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com
- Eng Platform / Change CAB: eng-platform@redwood.com

Appendix and links:
- Internal links to full templates, procurement system, ticketing forms, and security questionnaire are maintained in the Template Library (link internal).
- For questions or to request an exception to any policy, open a request with People Ops and include the policy section and justification.
